title: Puddle Jumping
Saltar charcos
task: Listen to the story about Noor. Retell it to someone using first, next and last.
Escucha el cuento sobre Noor. Vuelve a contarlo a alguien usando primero, después y al final.
frame: First, Noor ___. Next, she ___.
Primero, Noor ___. Después, ella ___.
lookFor: I told three parts of the story in order.
Conté tres partes del cuento en orden.
squares.listen: It was raining. First, Noor put on her yellow boots. Next, she went outside with her dad. She jumped in a big puddle. Splash! Her socks got wet. Last, they went home and drank warm cocoa.

title: The Lost Umbrella
El paraguas perdido
task: Read the story. Draw a picture for the beginning, the middle and the end, then tell how the problem was fixed.
Lee el cuento. Haz un dibujo del principio, del medio y del final, y luego di cómo se resolvió el problema.
frame: The problem was ___. Then ___.
El problema era ___. Luego ___.
lookFor: My three pictures show the problem and how it was fixed.
Mis tres dibujos muestran el problema y cómo se resolvió.
squares.read: Tom could not find his umbrella. It was raining hard. He looked under his bed. He looked in the closet. Then his sister said, Look by the door! The umbrella was there. Tom smiled and went to school.

title: My Rainy Day
Mi día de lluvia
task: Tell someone about a rainy day you remember. Say what you did first, then what happened next.
Cuéntale a alguien sobre un día de lluvia que recuerdes. Di qué hiciste primero y luego qué pasó después.
frame: One rainy day, I ___. Then I ___.
Un día de lluvia, yo ___. Luego yo ___.
lookFor: I used one rainy day and two time words.
Hablé de un día de lluvia y usé dos palabras de tiempo.

title: One Rainy Sentence
Una oración de lluvia
task: Write one sentence that tells what you like to do on a rainy day. Draw a picture to match.
Escribe una oración que diga qué te gusta hacer en un día de lluvia. Haz un dibujo que vaya con ella.
frame: On a rainy day, I ___.
En un día de lluvia, yo ___.
lookFor: My sentence has a capital letter, a period and matches my picture.
Mi oración tiene mayúscula, punto y va con mi dibujo.

title: Rain Comic
Historieta de lluvia
task: Fold a paper into three boxes. Draw a comic about a rainy day: before the rain, during the rain, after the rain. Tell the story out loud.
Dobla un papel en tres cuadros. Dibuja una historieta sobre un día de lluvia: antes de la lluvia, durante la lluvia y después de la lluvia. Cuenta la historia en voz alta.
frame: Before the rain, ___. After the rain, ___.
Antes de la lluvia, ___. Después de la lluvia, ___.
lookFor: My comic has three parts in order.
Mi historieta tiene tres partes en orden.

title: The Rainbow
El arcoíris
task: Listen to the story. Act out each thing Ama does, in the same order. Then say how the story ends.
Escucha el cuento. Actúa cada cosa que hace Ama, en el mismo orden. Luego di cómo termina el cuento.
frame: At the end, Ama ___.
Al final, Ama ___.
lookFor: I acted it out in order and told the ending.
Lo actué en orden y conté el final.
squares.listen: Ama looked out the window. Rain was falling. She read a book. She played a game with Grandma. After a while, the rain stopped. Ama ran to the window. She saw a rainbow in the sky!

title: Cat in the Rain
El gato bajo la lluvia
task: Read the story. Put three sticky notes or scraps of paper in a row and write one word on each for what happened first, next and last.
Lee el cuento. Pon tres papelitos en fila y escribe una palabra en cada uno sobre lo que pasó primero, después y al final.
frame: First, the cat ___. Last, it ___.
Primero, el gato ___. Al final, ___.
lookFor: My three words are in the right order.
Mis tres palabras están en el orden correcto.
squares.read: A little cat was on the porch. Drip, drop. Rain began to fall. The cat ran under a chair. A girl opened the door. The cat ran inside. It curled up on a soft blanket and went to sleep.

title: Rain Sounds Story
Cuento con sonidos de lluvia
task: Make up a story about a frog on a rainy day. Tell it with sounds, like drip, drop and splash, and use the words first and then.
Inventa un cuento sobre una rana en un día de lluvia. Cuéntalo con sonidos como plic, plac y splash, y usa las palabras primero y luego.
frame: First, the frog ___. Then ___.
Primero, la rana ___. Luego ___.
lookFor: My story has a beginning and an end.
Mi cuento tiene un principio y un final.

title: What Happened Next
Qué pasó después
task: Finish this story in one sentence: The rain stopped, and ___. Draw what happened.
Termina este cuento con una oración: Paró la lluvia y ___. Dibuja lo que pasó.
frame: When the rain stopped, I ___.
Cuando paró la lluvia, yo ___.
lookFor: My sentence tells what happened next.
Mi oración dice qué pasó después.

title: What Is a Bird?
¿Qué es un ave?
task: Listen to the facts about birds. Draw a bird and add the three body parts you heard.
Escucha los datos sobre las aves. Dibuja un ave y agrega las tres partes del cuerpo que escuchaste.
frame: A bird has ___ and ___.
Un ave tiene ___ y ___.
lookFor: My bird has feathers, wings and a beak.
Mi ave tiene plumas, alas y pico.
squares.listen: A bird is an animal. Every bird has feathers. Every bird has two wings and a beak. Birds hatch from eggs. Most birds can fly, but some birds, like penguins, cannot fly. Penguins swim instead.

title: The Hummingbird
El colibrí
task: Read about the hummingbird. Find two facts and tell them to someone at home.
Lee sobre el colibrí. Busca dos datos y cuéntaselos a alguien en casa.
frame: A hummingbird can ___.
Un colibrí puede ___.
lookFor: I told two true facts from the text.
Conté dos datos verdaderos del texto.
squares.read: The hummingbird is a very small bird. Its wings move so fast that they hum. A hummingbird can fly forward and backward. It drinks sweet juice from flowers with its long beak.

title: Bird Watch
Observa aves
task: Look out a window or think about a bird you have seen. Tell its color, its size and what it was doing.
Mira por la ventana o piensa en un ave que hayas visto. Di su color, su tamaño y qué estaba haciendo.
frame: The bird was ___. It was ___.
El ave era ___. Estaba ___.
lookFor: I told the color, the size and what it did.
Dije el color, el tamaño y qué hacía.

title: A Bird Fact
Un dato de aves
task: Write one sentence that tells a fact about birds. Start with Birds have or Birds can.
Escribe una oración que diga un dato sobre las aves. Empieza con Las aves tienen o Las aves pueden.
frame: Birds have ___.
Las aves tienen ___.
lookFor: My sentence tells something true about birds.
Mi oración dice algo verdadero sobre las aves.

title: Label a Bird
Rotula un ave
task: Draw a big bird. Write labels with lines for feathers, wings, beak and feet. Show it to someone and name each part.
Dibuja un ave grande. Escribe rótulos con líneas para plumas, alas, pico y patas. Muéstraselo a alguien y nombra cada parte.
frame: This part is the ___.
Esta parte es el ___.
lookFor: My bird has four labels in the right places.
Mi ave tiene cuatro rótulos en el lugar correcto.

title: Big Bird, Small Bird
Ave grande, ave pequeña
task: Listen to the facts. Hold your hands far apart for the ostrich and close together for the hummingbird. Say one way they are different.
Escucha los datos. Separa mucho las manos para el avestruz y júntalas para el colibrí. Di una forma en que son diferentes.
frame: The ostrich is ___, but the hummingbird is ___.
El avestruz es ___, pero el colibrí es ___.
lookFor: I said one difference.
Dije una diferencia.
squares.listen: The ostrich is the biggest bird. It is taller than a grown-up. It cannot fly, but it runs very fast. The hummingbird is one of the smallest birds. It is about as long as your finger.

title: Bird Nests
Nidos de aves
task: Read about nests. Make a list of the things birds use to build a nest.
Lee sobre los nidos. Haz una lista de las cosas que usan las aves para construir un nido.
frame: Birds use ___ to make a nest.
Las aves usan ___ para hacer un nido.
lookFor: My list has at least three things from the text.
Mi lista tiene por lo menos tres cosas del texto.
squares.read: Many birds build nests. A nest is a home for eggs and baby birds. Birds use sticks, grass, mud and leaves. Some birds put soft feathers inside. The nest keeps the eggs warm and safe.

title: Bird Expert
Experto en aves
task: Be a bird expert. Tell someone three facts about birds: what they have, what they can do and where they live.
Sé un experto en aves. Dile a alguien tres datos sobre las aves: qué tienen, qué pueden hacer y dónde viven.
frame: Birds have ___. Birds can ___.
Las aves tienen ___. Las aves pueden ___.
lookFor: I told three different facts.
Conté tres datos diferentes.

title: Same and Different
Igual y diferente
task: Write one sentence that tells how a bird and a dog are the same or different.
Escribe una oración que diga en qué se parecen o se diferencian un ave y un perro.
frame: A bird has ___, but a dog has ___.
Un ave tiene ___, pero un perro tiene ___.
lookFor: My sentence compares a bird and a dog.
Mi oración compara un ave y un perro.

theme: Por qué nos lavamos las manos

title: Germs on Hands
Microbios en las manos
task: Listen. Then tell someone why we wash our hands. Use the word because.
Escucha. Luego dile a alguien por qué nos lavamos las manos. Usa la palabra porque.
frame: We wash our hands because ___.
Nos lavamos las manos porque ___.
lookFor: I gave a reason with because.
Di una razón con porque.
squares.listen: Germs are tiny. They are so small that you cannot see them. Germs can get on your hands when you play. Some germs can make you sick. Soap and water wash the germs away.

title: Handwashing Steps
Pasos para lavarse las manos
task: Read the steps. Number them on a paper from 1 to 5, then act them out at a sink or pretend.
Lee los pasos. Numéralos en un papel del 1 al 5 y luego actúalos en un lavabo o de mentiritas.
frame: First, you ___. Then you ___.
Primero, tú ___. Luego tú ___.
lookFor: I did the steps in the right order.
Hice los pasos en el orden correcto.
squares.read: First, wet your hands with water. Next, put on soap. Then rub your hands together. Rub the backs and between your fingers too. After that, rinse off the soap. Last, dry your hands with a clean towel.

title: Teach a Friend
Enséñale a un amigo
task: Teach someone at home how to wash hands. Tell the steps in order and show each one.
Enséñale a alguien en casa cómo lavarse las manos. Di los pasos en orden y muestra cada uno.
frame: First, ___. Next, ___. Last, ___.
Primero, ___. Después, ___. Al final, ___.
lookFor: I told the steps in order.
Dije los pasos en orden.

title: When to Wash
Cuándo lavarse
task: Write one sentence that tells when you should wash your hands and why.
Escribe una oración que diga cuándo debes lavarte las manos y por qué.
frame: I wash my hands before I ___ because ___.
Me lavo las manos antes de ___ porque ___.
lookFor: My sentence says when and why.
Mi oración dice cuándo y por qué.

title: Clean Hands Sign
Cartel de manos limpias
task: Make a sign for a bathroom or kitchen. Draw the handwashing steps with numbers, and write one short line that says why.
Haz un cartel para el baño o la cocina. Dibuja los pasos para lavarse las manos con números y escribe una frase corta que diga por qué.
frame: Wash your hands so ___.
Lávate las manos para que ___.
lookFor: My sign shows the steps in order and a reason.
Mi cartel muestra los pasos en orden y una razón.

title: Soap Bubbles
Burbujas de jabón
task: Listen. Rub your hands together while you listen. Then say what soap does to germs.
Escucha. Frótate las manos mientras escuchas. Luego di qué le hace el jabón a los microbios.
frame: Soap helps because it ___.
El jabón ayuda porque ___.
lookFor: I said what soap does.
Dije qué hace el jabón.
squares.listen: Water alone does not wash away all the germs. Soap helps. When you rub soap on your hands, it makes bubbles. The soap grabs dirt and germs. Then the water rinses them down the drain.

title: Why Rub So Long?
¿Por qué frotar tanto?
task: Read the text. Find the reason we rub our hands for a long time, and tell it to someone.
Lee el texto. Busca la razón por la que nos frotamos las manos mucho tiempo y cuéntasela a alguien.
frame: We rub a long time so ___.
Frotamos mucho tiempo para que ___.
lookFor: I found the reason in the text.
Encontré la razón en el texto.
squares.read: Germs hide in small places. They hide between your fingers and under your nails. If you rub fast, you miss them. Rub your hands while you sing a short song two times. Then the soap can reach all the germs.

title: What If?
¿Qué pasaría si...?
task: Tell what could happen if someone did not wash their hands before eating. Use so or because.
Di qué podría pasar si alguien no se lavara las manos antes de comer. Usa así que o porque.
frame: If you do not wash, ___.
Si no te lavas, ___.
lookFor: I told what could happen and why.
Dije qué podría pasar y por qué.

title: Soap Sentence
Oración del jabón
task: Write one sentence that tells why we use soap. Draw your hands with bubbles.
Escribe una oración que diga por qué usamos jabón. Dibuja tus manos con burbujas.
frame: We use soap because ___.
Usamos jabón porque ___.
lookFor: My sentence gives a reason.
Mi oración da una razón.

theme: La mejor mascota para la clase

title: Fish or Hamster?
¿Pez o hámster?
task: Listen to two students. Say which pet each one wants and one reason each gives.
Escucha a dos estudiantes. Di qué mascota quiere cada uno y una razón que da cada uno.
frame: ___ wants a ___ because ___.
___ quiere un ___ porque ___.
lookFor: I said both pets and both reasons.
Dije las dos mascotas y las dos razones.
squares.listen: Maya says, We should get a fish. A fish is quiet, and it is fun to watch. Diego says, We should get a hamster. We can hold a hamster, and it can run on a wheel.

title: A Class Plant
Una planta para la clase
task: Read what Ji-woo thinks. Draw a circle around each reason on a paper copy or count them on your fingers.
Lee lo que piensa Ji-woo. Encierra cada razón en un círculo en una copia en papel o cuéntalas con los dedos.
frame: One reason is ___.
Una razón es ___.
lookFor: I found all of Ji-woo's reasons.
Encontré todas las razones de Ji-woo.
squares.read: I think a plant is the best class pet. It does not need food from a store. It only needs water and sun. It is quiet. It never runs away. We can watch it grow!

title: My Pick
Mi elección
task: Tell someone which class pet you would pick and give two reasons.
Dile a alguien qué mascota elegirías para la clase y da dos razones.
frame: I think a ___ is best because ___.
Creo que un ___ es el mejor porque ___.
lookFor: I gave my pick and two reasons.
Di mi elección y dos razones.

title: Pet Sentence
Oración de mascota
task: Write one sentence that tells your opinion about the best class pet and one reason.
Escribe una oración que diga tu opinión sobre la mejor mascota para la clase y una razón.
frame: The best class pet is a ___ because ___.
La mejor mascota para la clase es un ___ porque ___.
lookFor: My sentence has an opinion and a reason.
Mi oración tiene una opinión y una razón.

title: Vote for My Pet
Vota por mi mascota
task: Make a vote poster for your pet. Draw it, write its name, and add one reason. Ask two people at home to vote yes or no.
Haz un cartel de votación para tu mascota. Dibújala, escribe su nombre y agrega una razón. Pide a dos personas en casa que voten sí o no.
frame: Vote for the ___ because ___.
Vota por el ___ porque ___.
lookFor: My poster shows the pet and a reason.
Mi cartel muestra la mascota y una razón.

title: The Bunny Problem
El problema del conejo
task: Listen. Say one reason a bunny might be a good class pet and one reason it might not.
Escucha. Di una razón por la que un conejo podría ser una buena mascota para la clase y una razón por la que no.
frame: A bunny is good because ___. But ___.
Un conejo es bueno porque ___. Pero ___.
lookFor: I gave one good reason and one problem.
Di una razón buena y un problema.
squares.listen: A bunny is soft, and kids love to pet it. But a bunny needs a lot of space to hop. It also needs fresh food every day. Who will feed it on the weekend?

title: Which Reason Is Better?
¿Cuál razón es mejor?
task: Read the two reasons. Pick the one that is stronger and tell why.
Lee las dos razones. Elige la que es más fuerte y di por qué.
frame: The better reason is ___ because ___.
La mejor razón es ___ porque ___.
lookFor: I picked a reason and explained my pick.
Elegí una razón y expliqué por qué.
squares.read: We should get a fish. Reason one: Fish are blue. Reason two: A fish is easy to care for, because it only needs food and clean water. Which reason is better?

title: Two Sides
Dos lados
task: Pretend you and a friend want different pets. Say your pet and reason, then say why your friend's pet might be hard to care for.
Imagina que tú y un amigo quieren mascotas diferentes. Di tu mascota y tu razón, y luego di por qué la mascota de tu amigo podría ser difícil de cuidar.
frame: I want a ___. A ___ is hard because ___.
Yo quiero un ___. Un ___ es difícil porque ___.
lookFor: I gave my reason and talked about the other pet.
Di mi razón y hablé de la otra mascota.

title: Not That Pet
Esa mascota no
task: Write one sentence about a pet that would NOT be good for a class and why.
Escribe una oración sobre una mascota que NO sería buena para una clase y por qué.
frame: A ___ is not a good class pet because ___.
Un ___ no es una buena mascota para la clase porque ___.
lookFor: My sentence tells why not.
Mi oración dice por qué no.

title: Lina's Morning
La mañana de Lina
task: Listen to the story about Lina. Hold up one finger for each thing she does, then tell what she did first and what she did last.
Escucha el cuento sobre Lina. Levanta un dedo por cada cosa que hace y luego di qué hizo primero y qué hizo al final.
frame: First, Lina ___. Last, she ___.
Primero, Lina ___. Al final, ella ___.
lookFor: I said what Lina did first and last.
Dije qué hizo Lina primero y al final.
squares.listen: Lina wakes up. First, she brushes her teeth. Next, she eats rice and eggs. Then she puts on her shoes. Last, she walks to school with Grandpa.

title: Sam Gets Ready
Sam se prepara
task: A grown-up reads the story with you. Fold a paper into three boxes and draw what Sam does first, next and last.
Una persona adulta lee el cuento contigo. Dobla un papel en tres cuadros y dibuja lo que Sam hace primero, después y al final.
frame: First, Sam ___.
Primero, Sam ___.
lookFor: My three boxes are in the same order as the story.
Mis tres cuadros están en el mismo orden que el cuento.
squares.read: Sam gets up. He washes his face. He puts on a red shirt. He eats a banana. He waves goodbye to Mom.

title: Tell Your Morning
Cuenta tu mañana
task: Tell a grown-up three things you did this morning. Count on your fingers as you say first, next and last.
Cuéntale a una persona adulta tres cosas que hiciste esta mañana. Cuenta con los dedos mientras dices primero, después y al final.
frame: First, I ___. Next, I ___. Last, I ___.
Primero, yo ___. Después, yo ___. Al final, yo ___.
lookFor: I told three things in order.
Conté tres cosas en orden.

title: Draw and Label
Dibuja y escribe
task: Draw one thing you did this morning. Write or trace one word to label it, like eat, wash or dress.
Dibuja una cosa que hiciste esta mañana. Escribe o traza una palabra para nombrarla, como comer, lavar o vestir.
frame: This morning I ___.
Esta mañana yo ___.
lookFor: My picture shows one thing I did and has a word.
Mi dibujo muestra algo que hice y tiene una palabra.

title: My Morning Book
Mi libro de la mañana
task: Fold a paper in half to make a little book. Draw what you do first on the front and what you do last on the back, then read your book to someone at home.
Dobla un papel por la mitad para hacer un librito. Dibuja lo que haces primero en la portada y lo que haces al final atrás, y luego lee tu libro a alguien en casa.
frame: First I ___. Last I ___.
Primero yo ___. Al final yo ___.
lookFor: My book has a first page and a last page that match my morning.
Mi libro tiene una primera página y una última página que van con mi mañana.

title: Silly Ben
Ben el chistoso
task: Listen to the silly story about Ben. Act out what Ben does, in the same order.
Escucha el cuento chistoso sobre Ben. Actúa lo que hace Ben, en el mismo orden.
frame: Then Ben ___.
Después Ben ___.
lookFor: I acted out the story in the right order.
Actué el cuento en el orden correcto.
squares.listen: Ben was sleepy. He put his shoe on his hand! Ben laughed. Then he put the shoe on his foot. Last, he ran to the bus.

title: Act It Out
Actúalo
task: A grown-up reads each sentence. Point to the sentence and act it out. Then say what happens last.
Una persona adulta lee cada oración. Señala la oración y actúala. Luego di qué pasa al final.
frame: Last, I ___.
Al final, yo ___.
lookFor: I acted out every sentence and named the last one.
Actué cada oración y dije cuál es la última.
squares.read: I wake up. I make my bed. I eat bread and drink milk. I get my bag. I go to school.

title: A Pretend Morning
Una mañana imaginaria
task: Make up a pretend morning for a cat, a dog or a bird. Tell what it does first and then what it does next.
Inventa una mañana imaginaria para un gato, un perro o un pájaro. Di qué hace primero y qué hace después.
frame: First the ___ wakes up. Then it ___.
Primero el ___ se despierta. Después ___.
lookFor: I told what the animal did first and next.
Dije qué hizo el animal primero y después.

title: First and Last
Primero y al final
task: Draw two pictures: you waking up and you leaving home. Write or trace the word first under one and last under the other.
Haz dos dibujos: tú despertándote y tú saliendo de casa. Escribe o traza la palabra primero debajo de uno y al final debajo del otro.
frame: First I ___. Last I ___.
Primero yo ___. Al final yo ___.
lookFor: The word first is under the picture that happens first.
La palabra primero está debajo del dibujo que pasa primero.

title: The Orange
La naranja
task: Listen to the facts about an orange. Then point to something orange in your home and say one fact you heard.
Escucha los datos sobre la naranja. Luego señala algo anaranjado en tu casa y di un dato que escuchaste.
frame: An orange has ___.
Una naranja tiene ___.
lookFor: I said one true fact about an orange.
Dije un dato verdadero sobre la naranja.
squares.listen: An orange is a fruit. It is round. It has a thick peel. Inside, it has parts called sections. It tastes sweet and juicy.

title: Banana Facts
Datos del plátano
task: A grown-up reads the facts. Draw a banana and show its color and its peel. Tell one thing a banana has.
Una persona adulta lee los datos. Dibuja un plátano y muestra su color y su cáscara. Di una cosa que tiene el plátano.
frame: A banana is ___.
Un plátano es ___.
lookFor: My drawing matches the facts I heard.
Mi dibujo va con los datos que escuché.
squares.read: A banana is a fruit. It is long. It is yellow when it is ready to eat. You take off the peel. The inside is soft.

title: Name That Fruit
¿Qué fruta es?
task: Pick a fruit you know. Tell its color, its shape and how it tastes, and let someone at home guess the fruit.
Elige una fruta que conozcas. Di su color, su forma y su sabor, y deja que alguien en casa adivine la fruta.
frame: It is ___. It tastes ___.
Es ___. Sabe ___.
lookFor: I gave a color, a shape and a taste.
Dije un color, una forma y un sabor.

title: Label a Fruit
Ponle nombre a una fruta
task: Draw your favorite fruit. Write or trace its color word next to it.
Dibuja tu fruta favorita. Escribe o traza la palabra de su color al lado.
frame: My fruit is ___.
Mi fruta es ___.
lookFor: My fruit has a color word next to it.
Mi fruta tiene una palabra de color al lado.

title: Fruit Sort
Clasifica frutas
task: Draw four fruits on a paper. Draw a circle around the fruits that are round. Tell someone which fruits are round and which are not.
Dibuja cuatro frutas en un papel. Encierra en un círculo las frutas que son redondas. Dile a alguien cuáles son redondas y cuáles no.
frame: These fruits are ___.
Estas frutas son ___.
lookFor: I sorted my fruits into round and not round.
Separé mis frutas en redondas y no redondas.

title: Fruit Riddle
Adivinanza de fruta
task: Listen to the riddle. Draw the fruit you think it is, then say one clue that helped you.
Escucha la adivinanza. Dibuja la fruta que crees que es y luego di una pista que te ayudó.
frame: It is a ___ because it ___.
Es una ___ porque ___.
lookFor: I named the fruit and one clue.
Dije la fruta y una pista.
squares.listen: I am a fruit. I am red or green. I am round. I have a little stem on top. I crunch when you bite me. What am I?

title: Same and Different
Igual y diferente
task: A grown-up reads the sentences. Say one way a grape and a watermelon are the same and one way they are different.
Una persona adulta lee las oraciones. Di una forma en que una uva y una sandía son iguales y una en que son diferentes.
frame: Both are ___. A grape is ___.
Las dos son ___. Una uva es ___.
lookFor: I said one same thing and one different thing.
Dije algo igual y algo diferente.
squares.read: A grape is a fruit. A watermelon is a fruit too. A grape is small. A watermelon is big. Both are juicy.

title: Show and Tell
Muestra y cuenta
task: Find a fruit or vegetable at home, or draw one. Show it and tell two things about it.
Busca una fruta o una verdura en casa, o dibuja una. Muéstrala y di dos cosas sobre ella.
frame: This is a ___. It has ___.
Esto es ___. Tiene ___.
lookFor: I said what it is and one thing it has.
Dije qué es y algo que tiene.

title: Fruit Word
Palabra de fruta
task: Draw a fruit cut in half. Write or trace the word seed next to the seeds.
Dibuja una fruta cortada por la mitad. Escribe o traza la palabra semilla al lado de las semillas.
frame: My fruit has ___.
Mi fruta tiene ___.
lookFor: My drawing shows the seeds with a label.
Mi dibujo muestra las semillas con un nombre.

title: What a Seed Needs
Lo que necesita una semilla
task: Listen to how a seed grows. Hold up a finger for each thing the seed needs, then name them.
Escucha cómo crece una semilla. Levanta un dedo por cada cosa que necesita la semilla y luego nómbralas.
frame: A seed needs ___.
Una semilla necesita ___.
lookFor: I named the things a seed needs.
Nombré las cosas que necesita una semilla.
squares.listen: A seed goes in the soil. It needs water. It needs sun. First, a root grows down. Then a sprout grows up. Soon it is a plant.

title: Plant Steps
Pasos de la planta
task: A grown-up reads the steps. Draw the three steps in order: seed, sprout, plant.
Una persona adulta lee los pasos. Dibuja los tres pasos en orden: semilla, brote, planta.
frame: First it is a ___.
Primero es una ___.
lookFor: My drawings go seed, sprout, plant.
Mis dibujos van semilla, brote, planta.
squares.read: First, we plant a seed. Then we give it water. Next, a small sprout comes up. Last, it grows into a big plant.

title: Why Water?
¿Por qué agua?
task: Tell a grown-up why a plant needs water. Use the word because.
Dile a una persona adulta por qué una planta necesita agua. Usa la palabra porque.
frame: A plant needs water because ___.
Una planta necesita agua porque ___.
lookFor: I used the word because.
Usé la palabra porque.

title: Draw the Sun
Dibuja el sol
task: Draw a plant with the sun and rain. Write or trace one word: sun or rain.
Dibuja una planta con el sol y la lluvia. Escribe o traza una palabra: sol o lluvia.
frame: The plant gets ___.
La planta recibe ___.
lookFor: My picture shows what helps the plant grow.
Mi dibujo muestra lo que ayuda a la planta a crecer.

title: Grow Like a Seed
Crece como una semilla
task: Act out a seed growing: curl up small, get pretend rain and sun, then grow tall. Tell what made you grow.
Actúa como una semilla que crece: hazte bolita, recibe lluvia y sol de mentiritas y luego crece alto. Di qué te hizo crecer.
frame: I grew because I got ___.
Crecí porque recibí ___.
lookFor: I showed the steps and said what made me grow.
Mostré los pasos y dije qué me hizo crecer.

title: The Dry Plant
La planta seca
task: Listen to the story about a plant. Say what happened to it and why.
Escucha el cuento sobre una planta. Di qué le pasó y por qué.
frame: The plant was sad because ___.
La planta estaba triste porque ___.
lookFor: I said what happened and why.
Dije qué pasó y por qué.
squares.listen: Mia forgot to water her plant. The leaves got dry and droopy. Mia gave it water. The next day, the plant stood up tall.

title: Roots and Leaves
Raíces y hojas
task: A grown-up reads the sentences. Point to where roots are and where leaves are on a real plant or a drawing.
Una persona adulta lee las oraciones. Señala dónde están las raíces y dónde están las hojas en una planta de verdad o en un dibujo.
frame: Roots are ___.
Las raíces están ___.
lookFor: I pointed to the roots and the leaves.
Señalé las raíces y las hojas.
squares.read: A plant has roots. Roots are under the soil. Roots drink water. A plant has leaves. Leaves take in the sun.

title: Plant Helper
Ayudante de plantas
task: Pretend you are teaching a friend how to plant a seed. Tell the steps in order.
Imagina que le enseñas a un amigo cómo sembrar una semilla. Di los pasos en orden.
frame: First, ___. Then, ___.
Primero, ___. Después, ___.
lookFor: I told at least two steps in order.
Dije por lo menos dos pasos en orden.

title: Root Word
Palabra raíz
task: Draw a plant with roots under the ground. Write or trace the word root.
Dibuja una planta con raíces debajo de la tierra. Escribe o traza la palabra raíz.
frame: The roots are ___.
Las raíces están ___.
lookFor: My roots are under the ground and labeled.
Mis raíces están debajo de la tierra y tienen nombre.

title: Tag or Swings?
¿Atrapadas o columpios?
task: Listen to two friends. Point to the friend you agree with and say why.
Escucha a dos amigos. Señala al amigo con quien estás de acuerdo y di por qué.
frame: I like ___ because ___.
Me gusta ___ porque ___.
lookFor: I picked one and gave a reason.
Elegí uno y di una razón.
squares.listen: Ana says, I like tag best because I can run fast. Leo says, I like the swings best because I can fly high.

title: Jump Rope
Saltar la cuerda
task: A grown-up reads what Kai thinks. Say one reason Kai gives. Do you agree? Show thumbs up or thumbs down.
Una persona adulta lee lo que piensa Kai. Di una razón que da Kai. ¿Estás de acuerdo? Muestra pulgar arriba o pulgar abajo.
frame: Kai likes it because ___.
A Kai le gusta porque ___.
lookFor: I said Kai's reason and showed what I think.
Dije la razón de Kai y mostré lo que pienso.
squares.read: I think jump rope is the best game. You can play with lots of friends. You can sing songs. It makes you strong.

title: My Favorite Game
Mi juego favorito
task: Tell a grown-up your favorite playground game and one reason it is the best.
Dile a una persona adulta tu juego favorito del recreo y una razón por la que es el mejor.
frame: I think ___ is best because ___.
Creo que ___ es el mejor porque ___.
lookFor: I said my favorite and one reason.
Dije mi favorito y una razón.

title: Vote Card
Tarjeta de voto
task: Draw the game you like best. Write or trace the word yes next to it.
Dibuja el juego que más te gusta. Escribe o traza la palabra sí al lado.
frame: I vote for ___.
Yo voto por ___.
lookFor: My card shows one game and the word yes.
Mi tarjeta muestra un juego y la palabra sí.

title: Game Poster
Cartel del juego
task: Make a poster for your best game. Draw it and show a friend. Tell one reason they should play it.
Haz un cartel de tu mejor juego. Dibújalo y muéstraselo a un amigo. Dile una razón para que lo juegue.
frame: Play ___ because ___.
Juega ___ porque ___.
lookFor: My poster shows the game and I gave a reason.
Mi cartel muestra el juego y di una razón.

title: Sandbox Fan
Fan del arenero
task: Listen to why Rosa likes the sandbox. Hold up one finger for each reason.
Escucha por qué a Rosa le gusta el arenero. Levanta un dedo por cada razón.
frame: Rosa likes it because ___.
A Rosa le gusta porque ___.
lookFor: I counted Rosa's reasons.
Conté las razones de Rosa.
squares.listen: Rosa says the sandbox is the best. She can build a castle. She can dig a big hole. She can play with her brother.

title: Which Is Better?
¿Cuál es mejor?
task: A grown-up reads the sentences. Say which game the child thinks is better and the reason.
Una persona adulta lee las oraciones. Di qué juego cree el niño que es mejor y la razón.
frame: He thinks ___ is better.
Él cree que ___ es mejor.
lookFor: I said the game and the reason.
Dije el juego y la razón.
squares.read: Ball games are fun. Slides are fun too. Omar thinks the slide is better. It goes fast. Whee!

title: Change My Mind
Hazme cambiar de idea
task: Pick a game. Try to get someone at home to want to play it. Give two reasons.
Elige un juego. Trata de que alguien en casa quiera jugarlo. Da dos razones.
frame: You should play ___ because ___.
Deberías jugar ___ porque ___.
lookFor: I gave two reasons.
Di dos razones.

title: Thumbs Up
Pulgar arriba
task: Draw a game you like and a game you do not like. Write or trace yes under one and no under the other.
Dibuja un juego que te gusta y un juego que no te gusta. Escribe o traza sí debajo de uno y no debajo del otro.
frame: I like ___. I do not like ___.
Me gusta ___. No me gusta ___.
lookFor: My yes and no match what I think.
Mi sí y mi no van con lo que pienso.

title: Grandma's Party
La fiesta de la abuela
task: Listen to the story. On paper, write four time words you hear (like first or then), then use them to retell the story.
Escucha el cuento. En un papel, escribe cuatro palabras de tiempo que escuches (como primero o luego) y úsalas para volver a contar el cuento.
frame: First, the family ___. After that, ___.
Primero, la familia ___. Después de eso, ___.
lookFor: I used the time words to retell the events in order.
Usé las palabras de tiempo para volver a contar los sucesos en orden.
squares.listen: It was Grandma's birthday. First, Marco and his mom made tamales in the kitchen. Then his cousins came with balloons. After that, everyone hid behind the couch. When Grandma opened the door, they all shouted, Surprise! Grandma laughed so hard she cried happy tears. At the end of the night, the whole family danced in the living room.

title: The Big Cake
El gran pastel
task: Read the story. Draw a story map with three boxes: the problem, what the characters did, and how it ended.
Lee el cuento. Haz un mapa del cuento con tres cuadros: el problema, lo que hicieron los personajes y cómo terminó.
frame: The problem was ___. They fixed it by ___.
El problema era ___. Lo resolvieron ___.
lookFor: My map shows the problem and the solution.
Mi mapa muestra el problema y la solución.
squares.read: Amira and her dad baked a big cake for the family picnic. They put it in the car. On the way, the car hit a bump. Oh no! The top of the cake slid off. Amira had an idea. When they got to the park, she put fresh strawberries all over the top. Everyone said it was the best cake ever.

title: Tell a Celebration
Cuenta una celebración
task: Tell someone about a celebration you went to. Say who was there, what happened in order, and how it ended.
Cuéntale a alguien sobre una celebración a la que fuiste. Di quién estaba, qué pasó en orden y cómo terminó.
frame: At the celebration, first ___. Then ___. At the end, ___.
En la celebración, primero ___. Luego ___. Al final, ___.
lookFor: I told who, what happened in order, and the ending.
Dije quién estaba, qué pasó en orden y el final.

title: My Favorite Moment
Mi momento favorito
task: Write 2 or 3 sentences about your favorite moment at a celebration. Use one time word and tell how you felt.
Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones sobre tu momento favorito en una celebración. Usa una palabra de tiempo y di cómo te sentiste.
frame: One time at a celebration, ___. I felt ___ because ___.
Una vez en una celebración, ___. Me sentí ___ porque ___.
lookFor: My sentences tell what happened and how I felt.
Mis oraciones dicen qué pasó y cómo me sentí.

title: Celebration Interview
Entrevista de celebración
task: Interview someone at home about a celebration they remember. Ask: What happened first? What happened next? How did it end? Draw one picture of their story and retell it.
Entrevista a alguien en casa sobre una celebración que recuerde. Pregunta: ¿Qué pasó primero? ¿Qué pasó después? ¿Cómo terminó? Haz un dibujo de su historia y vuelve a contarla.
frame: My ___ remembers when ___.
Mi ___ recuerda cuando ___.
lookFor: I retold their story in order.
Volví a contar su historia en orden.

title: The Lantern Walk
El paseo de faroles
task: Listen to the story. Act out the events in order, then tell the most important moment.
Escucha el cuento. Actúa los sucesos en orden y luego di cuál fue el momento más importante.
frame: The most important moment was when ___.
El momento más importante fue cuando ___.
lookFor: I acted it out in order and named the big moment.
Lo actué en orden y dije el momento importante.
squares.listen: On the night of the festival, Lin and her brother made paper lanterns. First, they folded red paper. Next, they painted gold stars on the sides. When it got dark, their uncle helped them put a small light inside. Then the whole family walked down the street. Lin held her lantern up high. It glowed like the moon.

title: Wedding Day Mix-Up
Lío en la boda
task: Read the story. Write the four events on strips of paper, mix them up, then put them back in order.
Lee el cuento. Escribe los cuatro sucesos en tiras de papel, mézclalas y luego ponlas otra vez en orden.
frame: First, ___. Next, ___. Then, ___. Finally, ___.
Primero, ___. Después, ___. Luego, ___. Por último, ___.
lookFor: My strips are in the same order as the story.
Mis tiras están en el mismo orden que el cuento.
squares.read: At his aunt's wedding, Kofi had one job. He had to carry the rings. First, he put on his new shirt. Next, he walked to the front very slowly. Then he looked down. The ring box was empty! Kofi's heart pounded. Finally, he found the rings in his pocket, right where Mom had put them.

title: Act It Out
Actúalo
task: With someone at home, act out a short scene from a family celebration. Then tell the story in order using first, next and finally.
Con alguien en casa, actúa una escena corta de una celebración familiar. Luego cuenta la historia en orden usando primero, después y por último.
frame: First, we ___. Next, ___. Finally, ___.
Primero, nosotros ___. Después, ___. Por último, ___.
lookFor: I used three time words in order.
Usé tres palabras de tiempo en orden.

title: A Different Ending
Un final diferente
task: Think of a celebration story you know or just heard. Write 2 or 3 sentences that give it a new ending.
Piensa en un cuento de celebración que conozcas o que acabas de escuchar. Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones con un final nuevo.
frame: Suddenly, ___. In the end, ___.
De repente, ___. Al final, ___.
lookFor: My ending makes sense with the story.
Mi final tiene sentido con el cuento.

title: What Is a Desert?
¿Qué es un desierto?
task: Listen to the facts. Fold a paper in half: write What a desert is on one side and Desert plants and animals on the other. Add one fact to each side.
Escucha los datos. Dobla un papel por la mitad: escribe Qué es un desierto en un lado y Plantas y animales del desierto en el otro. Agrega un dato a cada lado.
frame: A desert is a place that ___.
Un desierto es un lugar que ___.
lookFor: Each fact is on the correct side.
Cada dato está en el lado correcto.
squares.listen: A desert is a place that gets very little rain. Some deserts are hot, and some deserts are cold. In a hot desert, the days are very hot, but the nights can be chilly. Desert plants and animals have special ways to live with little water. A cactus stores water inside its thick stem.

title: The Camel
El camello
task: Read about camels. Make a list of three body parts and what each one helps the camel do.
Lee sobre los camellos. Haz una lista de tres partes del cuerpo y lo que cada una ayuda al camello a hacer.
frame: A camel has ___ that help it ___.
El camello tiene ___ que lo ayudan a ___.
lookFor: Each part on my list has a job.
Cada parte de mi lista tiene una función.
squares.read: A camel is a desert animal. Many people think its hump is full of water, but it is full of fat. The camel can use this fat for energy when there is little food. Camels have long eyelashes that keep out blowing sand. They also have wide feet that help them walk on soft sand without sinking.

title: Desert or Forest?
¿Desierto o bosque?
task: Tell someone two ways a desert is different from a forest. Use but or different.
Dile a alguien dos formas en que un desierto es diferente de un bosque. Usa pero o diferente.
frame: A desert has ___, but a forest has ___.
Un desierto tiene ___, pero un bosque tiene ___.
lookFor: I compared the desert and the forest two ways.
Comparé el desierto y el bosque de dos formas.

title: Desert Facts
Datos del desierto
task: Write 2 or 3 sentences that teach a younger child about deserts. Tell what a desert is and give one example of a desert plant or animal.
Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones para enseñarle a un niño más pequeño sobre los desiertos. Di qué es un desierto y da un ejemplo de una planta o un animal del desierto.
frame: A desert is ___. For example, ___.
Un desierto es ___. Por ejemplo, ___.
lookFor: My sentences define a desert and give an example.
Mis oraciones definen un desierto y dan un ejemplo.

title: Desert Fact Card
Tarjeta de datos del desierto
task: Make a fact card about one desert animal or plant. Draw it, label two body parts, and write one fact at the bottom. Present it to someone.
Haz una tarjeta de datos sobre un animal o una planta del desierto. Dibújalo, rotula dos partes del cuerpo y escribe un dato abajo. Preséntala a alguien.
frame: This is a ___. It has ___.
Este es un ___. Tiene ___.
lookFor: My card has a drawing, two labels and a fact.
Mi tarjeta tiene un dibujo, dos rótulos y un dato.

title: The Fennec Fox
El zorro del desierto
task: Listen to the facts. Draw the fennec fox and label the body part that helps it stay cool.
Escucha los datos. Dibuja al zorro del desierto y rotula la parte del cuerpo que lo ayuda a mantenerse fresco.
frame: Its ___ help it stay cool.
Sus ___ lo ayudan a mantenerse fresco.
lookFor: I labeled the ears as the cooling part.
Rotulé las orejas como la parte que lo refresca.
squares.listen: The fennec fox is the smallest fox in the world. It lives in the Sahara Desert in Africa. It has very big ears. Its ears let heat leave its body, so the fox stays cool. The fox sleeps in a burrow during the hot day. At night, when it is cooler, it comes out to hunt.

title: Cactus Parts
Partes del cactus
task: Read about the cactus. Draw a cactus and label three parts with what each part does.
Lee sobre el cactus. Dibuja un cactus y rotula tres partes con lo que hace cada parte.
frame: The ___ helps the cactus ___.
El ___ ayuda al cactus a ___.
lookFor: Each label tells what the part does.
Cada rótulo dice lo que hace la parte.
squares.read: A cactus is a plant that lives in dry places. Its thick stem stores water for a long time. Its sharp spines keep animals from eating it. Its roots spread out wide, close to the top of the ground, so they can soak up rain quickly. Some cactuses grow bright flowers.

title: Animal Report
Informe de animal
task: Give a short talk about one desert animal. Tell what it is, where it lives and one way it survives with little water.
Da una charla corta sobre un animal del desierto. Di qué es, dónde vive y una forma en que sobrevive con poca agua.
frame: The ___ is a kind of ___. It lives ___.
El ___ es un tipo de ___. Vive ___.
lookFor: I told what it is, where it lives, and how it survives.
Dije qué es, dónde vive y cómo sobrevive.

title: Hot and Cold Deserts
Desiertos calientes y fríos
task: Write 2 or 3 sentences that tell how hot deserts and cold deserts are the same and how they are different.
Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones que digan en qué se parecen y en qué se diferencian los desiertos calientes y los fríos.
frame: Both deserts ___. A hot desert ___, but a cold desert ___.
Los dos desiertos ___. Un desierto caliente ___, pero un desierto frío ___.
lookFor: I wrote one way they are the same and one way they are different.
Escribí una forma en que se parecen y una en que se diferencian.

title: Where Puddles Go
A dónde van los charcos
task: Listen. Then explain to someone what happens to a puddle on a sunny day and why.
Escucha. Luego explícale a alguien qué le pasa a un charco en un día de sol y por qué.
frame: The puddle ___ because ___.
El charco ___ porque ___.
lookFor: I said what happens and the cause.
Dije qué pasa y la causa.
squares.listen: After a rainstorm, there is a big puddle on the sidewalk. Then the sun comes out. The sun warms the water. When water gets warm, it turns into a gas called water vapor. The vapor rises into the air. You cannot see it. Little by little, the puddle gets smaller until it is gone.

title: Cloud to Rain
De nube a lluvia
task: Read the text. Draw a circle with four arrows and write one step of the water cycle at each arrow, in order.
Lee el texto. Dibuja un círculo con cuatro flechas y escribe un paso del ciclo del agua en cada flecha, en orden.
frame: First, water ___. Then ___.
Primero, el agua ___. Luego ___.
lookFor: My circle shows the four steps in order.
Mi círculo muestra los cuatro pasos en orden.
squares.read: Water moves in a cycle. First, the sun warms water in oceans and lakes, and it rises as vapor. This is evaporation. Next, the vapor cools high in the sky and forms tiny drops. The drops make clouds. This is condensation. Then the drops get heavy and fall as rain or snow. This is precipitation. Last, the water collects in oceans and lakes again.

title: Explain the Fog
Explica la niebla
task: Breathe on a cold window or mirror. Explain to someone why it gets foggy, using because.
Echa tu aliento en una ventana o un espejo frío. Explícale a alguien por qué se empaña, usando porque.
frame: It gets foggy because ___.
Se empaña porque ___.
lookFor: I linked the cold glass to the water drops.
Relacioné el vidrio frío con las gotas de agua.

title: Why It Rains
Por qué llueve
task: Write 2 or 3 sentences that explain why it rains. Use the words so or because.
Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones que expliquen por qué llueve. Usa las palabras así que o porque.
frame: Drops in a cloud get ___, so ___.
Las gotas de una nube se ponen ___, así que ___.
lookFor: My sentences tell the cause and the effect.
Mis oraciones dicen la causa y el efecto.

title: Water Cycle Show
Función del ciclo del agua
task: Act out the water cycle as a water drop. Show each step with your body and say what makes you move to the next step.
Actúa el ciclo del agua como una gota de agua. Muestra cada paso con el cuerpo y di qué te hace pasar al siguiente paso.
frame: The sun warms me, so I ___.
El sol me calienta, así que yo ___.
lookFor: I acted every step and said each cause.
Actué cada paso y dije cada causa.

title: The Cold Glass
El vaso frío
task: Listen. Then tell what caused the water drops on the outside of the glass.
Escucha. Luego di qué causó las gotas de agua por fuera del vaso.
frame: The drops formed because ___.
Las gotas se formaron porque ___.
lookFor: I named the cause: warm air touched the cold glass.
Dije la causa: el aire tibio tocó el vaso frío.
squares.listen: On a hot day, Sofi poured ice water into a glass. A few minutes later, the outside of the glass was wet. Did the glass leak? No! The air around the glass had water vapor in it. When the warm air touched the cold glass, the vapor cooled and turned back into tiny drops. This is condensation.

title: Snow or Rain?
¿Nieve o lluvia?
task: Read the text. Fill in a two-column chart: Rain on one side and Snow on the other. Write what causes each.
Lee el texto. Completa una tabla de dos columnas: Lluvia en un lado y Nieve en el otro. Escribe qué causa cada una.
frame: When the air is ___, water falls as ___.
Cuando el aire está ___, el agua cae como ___.
lookFor: My chart shows the cause for rain and for snow.
Mi tabla muestra la causa de la lluvia y de la nieve.
squares.read: Water falls from clouds in different ways. When the air is warm, the drops fall as rain. When the air is very cold, the water in the clouds freezes into ice crystals. The crystals stick together and fall as snowflakes. So the temperature of the air decides if we get rain or snow.

title: Teach It
Enséñalo
task: Teach someone at home the water cycle. Point to a drawing or use your hands and say what causes each step.
Enséñale a alguien en casa el ciclo del agua. Señala un dibujo o usa las manos y di qué causa cada paso.
frame: When the vapor cools, ___.
Cuando el vapor se enfría, ___.
lookFor: I explained each step with a cause.
Expliqué cada paso con una causa.

title: Drying Clothes
Ropa que se seca
task: Wet clothes on a line get dry. Write 2 or 3 sentences that explain where the water goes and why.
La ropa mojada en un tendedero se seca. Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones que expliquen a dónde va el agua y por qué.
frame: The clothes get dry because ___. The water ___.
La ropa se seca porque ___. El agua ___.
lookFor: I used the word evaporation or explained it.
Usé la palabra evaporación o la expliqué.

title: Two Views
Dos opiniones
task: Listen to two students. Make a T-chart labeled Yes and No and write each student's reasons on the correct side.
Escucha a dos estudiantes. Haz una tabla en T con Sí y No, y escribe las razones de cada estudiante en el lado correcto.
frame: ___ thinks ___ because ___.
___ piensa que ___ porque ___.
lookFor: Each reason is under the right opinion.
Cada razón está debajo de la opinión correcta.
squares.listen: Luis thinks recess should be longer. He says that playing outside helps kids get exercise. He also says that kids pay better attention in class after they run and play. Hana does not agree. She thinks recess is long enough. She says that if recess is longer, there will be less time to learn math and reading.

title: A Letter to the Principal
Una carta a la directora
task: Read the letter. Find the opinion and underline or copy it. Then list the two reasons.
Lee la carta. Busca la opinión y subráyala o cópiala. Luego haz una lista de las dos razones.
frame: The writer believes ___. One reason is ___.
La persona que escribe cree que ___. Una razón es ___.
lookFor: I found the opinion and both reasons.
Encontré la opinión y las dos razones.
squares.read: Dear Principal, I believe our recess should be longer. One reason is that kids need time to move their bodies. Running and playing keep us healthy. Another reason is that recess helps us make friends. We learn to share, take turns and solve problems together. Please give us ten more minutes to play. Sincerely, Room 12

title: Your Opinion
Tu opinión
task: Tell someone if you think recess should be longer. Give your opinion and two reasons.
Dile a alguien si piensas que el recreo debería durar más. Da tu opinión y dos razones.
frame: I think recess should ___. One reason is ___. Another reason is ___.
Pienso que el recreo debería ___. Una razón es ___. Otra razón es ___.
lookFor: I gave an opinion and two reasons.
Di una opinión y dos razones.

title: Opinion Note
Nota de opinión
task: Write 2 or 3 sentences to your teacher about recess. Say your opinion and give a reason with an example.
Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones a tu maestro sobre el recreo. Di tu opinión y da una razón con un ejemplo.
frame: I think ___ because ___. For example, ___.
Pienso que ___ porque ___. Por ejemplo, ___.
lookFor: My note has an opinion, a reason and an example.
Mi nota tiene una opinión, una razón y un ejemplo.

title: Recess Poll
Encuesta del recreo
task: Ask three people at home or in class: Should recess be longer? Make tally marks for yes and no and write one reason you heard. Tell what most people think.
Pregunta a tres personas en casa o en clase: ¿Debería durar más el recreo? Haz marcas de conteo para sí y no, y escribe una razón que escuchaste. Di qué piensa la mayoría.
frame: Most people said ___ because ___.
La mayoría dijo ___ porque ___.
lookFor: My poll shows the answers and one reason.
Mi encuesta muestra las respuestas y una razón.

title: The Indoor Recess Idea
La idea del recreo adentro
task: Listen. Say the speaker's idea, then say if you agree and why.
Escucha. Di la idea de quien habla y luego di si estás de acuerdo y por qué.
frame: The speaker thinks ___. I agree because ___.
Quien habla piensa que ___. Estoy de acuerdo porque ___.
lookFor: I said the idea and my own opinion with a reason.
Dije la idea y mi propia opinión con una razón.
squares.listen: On rainy days, we stay inside for recess. I think indoor recess should have more choices. Right now, we can only draw. If we had board games and building blocks, more kids would have fun. Kids could also work together in teams. That is why I think indoor recess needs more choices.

title: Strong or Weak?
¿Fuerte o débil?
task: Read the three reasons. Mark the strongest reason with a star and the weakest with an X. Tell why.
Lee las tres razones. Marca la razón más fuerte con una estrella y la más débil con una X. Di por qué.
frame: The strongest reason is ___ because ___.
La razón más fuerte es ___ porque ___.
lookFor: I picked the strongest reason and explained why.
Elegí la razón más fuerte y expliqué por qué.
squares.read: Jada wants a longer recess. Here are her reasons. Reason A: Recess is fun. Reason B: Doctors say kids need at least one hour of exercise every day, and recess gives us time to move. Reason C: My friend wants it too. Which reason gives the best support for her opinion?

title: Debate a Partner
Debate con un compañero
task: Pick a side: longer recess or not. Tell your reason. Then have someone give the other side, and answer them.
Elige un lado: recreo más largo o no. Di tu razón. Luego pide a alguien que dé el otro lado y respóndele.
frame: I understand ___, but I still think ___ because ___.
Entiendo que ___, pero sigo pensando que ___ porque ___.
lookFor: I gave a reason and answered the other side.
Di una razón y respondí al otro lado.

title: The Other Side
El otro lado
task: Write 2 or 3 sentences giving a reason for the side you do NOT agree with. Then say why you still keep your opinion.
Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones con una razón del lado con el que NO estás de acuerdo. Luego di por qué sigues con tu opinión.
frame: Some people think ___. But I think ___ because ___.
Algunas personas piensan que ___. Pero yo pienso que ___ porque ___.
lookFor: I wrote the other side and my own reason.
Escribí el otro lado y mi propia razón.

title: The Missing Notebook
El cuaderno perdido
task: Listen to the story. Draw a timeline with five points and write one event at each point, then circle the most important moment.
Escucha el cuento. Dibuja una línea de tiempo con cinco puntos y escribe un suceso en cada punto; luego encierra en un círculo el momento más importante.
frame: First, ___. Suddenly, ___. Finally, ___.
Primero, ___. De repente, ___. Por último, ___.
lookFor: My timeline is in order and I circled the turning point.
Mi línea de tiempo está en orden y encerré el momento clave.
squares.listen: One Monday morning, Dev reached into his backpack for his science notebook. It was not there. His stomach dropped, because his whole bean plant project was inside. First, he checked his desk. Next, he looked in the cubbies and under the reading rug. Then he remembered that he had worked in the library on Friday. Dev asked his teacher if he could go check. The librarian smiled and held up a green notebook. Someone had turned it in to the lost and found. Finally, Dev hugged the notebook and promised himself he would always write his first name inside the cover.

title: Buddy Comes Home
Buddy vuelve a casa
task: Read the story. Make a story map: setting, characters, problem, three events and solution.
Lee el cuento. Haz un mapa del cuento: ambiente, personajes, problema, tres sucesos y solución.
frame: The problem was ___. It was solved when ___.
El problema era ___. Se resolvió cuando ___.
lookFor: My map has every part, and the events are in order.
Mi mapa tiene todas las partes y los sucesos están en orden.
squares.read: One windy afternoon, Paola's little dog, Buddy, slipped out of the gate. Paola and her grandfather searched up and down the street, calling his name. At first, they found nothing. Then Paola had an idea. She drew a picture of Buddy and wrote FOUND A DOG? CALL OUR BUILDING OFFICE. Her grandfather helped her tape copies to light poles. After that, they waited by the window. The sun was setting when a neighbor knocked on the door. Buddy was in her arms, wagging his tail. He had been sleeping on her porch the whole time. At the end of the day, Paola gave her neighbor a thank-you card.

title: A Time I Lost Something
Una vez que perdí algo
task: Tell someone about a time you lost something and found it, or make one up. Include where you were, what you did in order, and how you felt at the end.
Cuéntale a alguien sobre una vez que perdiste algo y lo encontraste, o invéntalo. Incluye dónde estabas, qué hiciste en orden y cómo te sentiste al final.
frame: One day, I could not find my ___. First, I ___. Then ___. At the end, I felt ___.
Un día, no podía encontrar mi ___. Primero, yo ___. Luego ___. Al final, me sentí ___.
lookFor: I told the setting, the events in order and my feelings.
Conté el lugar, los sucesos en orden y mis sentimientos.

title: Lost and Found Paragraph
Párrafo de perdido y encontrado
task: Write a paragraph of 3 to 5 sentences about a lost object that finds its way home. Use at least three signal words such as first, then, suddenly or finally.
Escribe un párrafo de 3 a 5 oraciones sobre un objeto perdido que vuelve a casa. Usa por lo menos tres palabras de transición como primero, luego, de repente o por último.
frame: One day, ___ was lost. Then ___. Suddenly, ___. Finally, ___.
Un día, ___ se perdió. Luego ___. De repente, ___. Por último, ___.
lookFor: My paragraph has a beginning, a problem, an ending and three signal words.
Mi párrafo tiene principio, problema, final y tres palabras de transición.

title: The Object Tells Its Story
El objeto cuenta su historia
task: Pick an object at home, like a sock or a spoon. Draw a four-panel comic where the object tells how it got lost and found, with speech bubbles. Read it aloud to someone.

Elige un objeto de tu casa, como un calcetín o una cuchara. Dibuja una historieta de cuatro cuadros donde el objeto cuenta cómo se perdió y lo encontraron, con globos de diálogo. Léela en voz alta a alguien.
frame: I am a ___. One day, I ___. Then ___.
Soy un ___. Un día, yo ___. Luego ___.
lookFor: My comic tells the events in order from the object's point of view.
Mi historieta cuenta los sucesos en orden desde el punto de vista del objeto.

title: The Lost Kite
El papalote perdido
task: Listen to the story. Retell it to someone in four sentences, using a different signal word to start each sentence.
Escucha el cuento. Vuelve a contarlo a alguien en cuatro oraciones y empieza cada oración con una palabra de transición diferente.
frame: At first, ___. After that, ___. Then ___. In the end, ___.
Al principio, ___. Después de eso, ___. Luego ___. Al final, ___.
lookFor: Each of my four sentences starts with a different signal word.
Cada una de mis cuatro oraciones empieza con una palabra de transición diferente.
squares.listen: On the first warm day of spring, Ayo and her cousin flew a red kite at the park. At first, the kite danced high above the trees. Then a strong gust of wind pulled the string right out of Ayo's hands. The kite sailed over the fence and disappeared. The girls ran to the other side, but they could not find it anywhere. After that, they walked home sadly. The next morning, Ayo's cousin shouted from the window. The red kite was stuck in the tree outside their apartment building! Their neighbor used a long pole to free it, and the girls cheered.

title: Grandpa's Watch
El reloj del abuelo
task: Read the story. Write the sentence where the problem starts and the sentence where it is solved. Then explain how the character changed.
Lee el cuento. Escribe la oración donde empieza el problema y la oración donde se resuelve. Luego explica cómo cambió el personaje.
frame: At the beginning, Sami felt ___. At the end, he felt ___.
Al principio, Sami se sentía ___. Al final, se sentía ___.
lookFor: I found both sentences and described the change.
Encontré las dos oraciones y describí el cambio.
squares.read: Sami's grandfather gave him a special gift: an old silver watch that had belonged to Sami's great-grandfather. Sami wore it to the beach on Saturday. When he got home, his wrist was bare. He had lost the watch! Sami felt terrible. He did not want to tell anyone. That night, he finally told his grandfather the truth. Grandpa hugged him and said, Things can be lost, but you were honest. The next weekend, they went back to the beach together. While they were walking, Sami saw something shiny near the lifeguard stand. It was the watch, safe in the lost and found box.

title: Radio Report
Reporte de radio
task: Pretend you are a radio reporter telling a lost-and-found story from your neighborhood. Tell it in order, include what someone said, and end with how it worked out.
Imagina que eres reportero de radio y cuentas una historia de perdido y encontrado de tu barrio. Cuéntala en orden, incluye lo que dijo alguien y termina con cómo se resolvió.
frame: This morning, ___. A neighbor said, ___. In the end, ___.
Esta mañana, ___. Un vecino dijo: ___. Al final, ___.
lookFor: My report is in order and includes what someone said.
Mi reporte está en orden e incluye lo que dijo alguien.

title: What Did They Learn?
¿Qué aprendieron?
task: Choose one lost-and-found story on this board. Write a paragraph of 3 to 5 sentences that retells it and ends with what the character learned.
Elige un cuento de perdido y encontrado de este tablero. Escribe un párrafo de 3 a 5 oraciones que lo vuelva a contar y termine con lo que aprendió el personaje.
frame: In the story, ___. After that, ___. In the end, ___ learned that ___.
En el cuento, ___. Después de eso, ___. Al final, ___ aprendió que ___.
lookFor: My paragraph retells the events and names a lesson.
Mi párrafo vuelve a contar los sucesos y dice una lección.

title: Layers of the Rain Forest
Las capas del bosque tropical
task: Listen. Draw a tall tree and divide it into four layers. Label each layer and write one fact about it.
Escucha. Dibuja un árbol alto y divídelo en cuatro capas. Rotula cada capa y escribe un dato sobre ella.
frame: The ___ layer has ___.
La capa del ___ tiene ___.
lookFor: My four layers are in order from top to bottom with one fact each.
Mis cuatro capas están en orden de arriba abajo con un dato cada una.
squares.listen: A tropical rain forest is a warm, wet forest that grows near the equator. Scientists describe it in four layers. The emergent layer is at the very top, where a few giant trees poke out above the rest. Below it is the canopy, a thick roof of leaves and branches. Many animals, such as monkeys and toucans, live here. Next is the understory, a shady place with small trees and bushes. At the bottom is the forest floor. It is dark because very little sunlight reaches it. Fallen leaves rot quickly there and feed the soil.

title: The Sloth
El perezoso
task: Read about sloths. Sort the facts into a chart with three columns: Body, Food and Habits.
Lee sobre los perezosos. Clasifica los datos en una tabla de tres columnas: Cuerpo, Comida y Costumbres.
frame: A sloth has ___. It eats ___. It also ___.
El perezoso tiene ___. Come ___. También ___.
lookFor: Every fact is in the right column.
Cada dato está en la columna correcta.
squares.read: The sloth is a mammal that lives in the rain forests of Central and South America. It spends almost its whole life hanging upside down in the trees. Sloths have long, curved claws that work like hooks on branches. They eat mostly leaves. Leaves do not give much energy, so sloths move very slowly and sleep many hours a day. Tiny green plants called algae grow in a sloth's fur. The green color helps the sloth blend in with the leaves. About once a week, a sloth climbs down to the ground.

title: Rain Forest Expert
Experto en bosques tropicales
task: Give a short talk to someone at home about rain forests. Name the topic, give three facts grouped together, and close with the main point.
Da una charla corta a alguien en casa sobre los bosques tropicales. Di el tema, da tres datos agrupados y termina con la idea principal.
frame: A rain forest is a kind of ___. It has ___. In addition, ___.
Un bosque tropical es un tipo de ___. Tiene ___. Además, ___.
lookFor: I named the topic, gave three facts and ended with the main point.
Dije el tema, di tres datos y terminé con la idea principal.

title: Informative Paragraph
Párrafo informativo
task: Write a paragraph of 3 to 5 sentences about one rain forest animal or plant. Use is a kind of, has and for example.
Escribe un párrafo de 3 a 5 oraciones sobre un animal o una planta del bosque tropical. Usa es un tipo de, tiene y por ejemplo.
frame: A ___ is a kind of ___. It has ___. For example, ___. In conclusion, ___.
Un ___ es un tipo de ___. Tiene ___. Por ejemplo, ___. En conclusión, ___.
lookFor: My paragraph defines it, gives details and closes with a main point.
Mi párrafo lo define, da detalles y termina con una idea principal.

title: Mini Field Guide
Mini guía de campo
task: Fold a paper into a four-page booklet. Make a field guide with one rain forest layer per page: draw an animal that lives there and write one fact. Read it to someone.
Dobla un papel para hacer un librito de cuatro páginas. Haz una guía de campo con una capa del bosque tropical por página: dibuja un animal que vive ahí y escribe un dato. Léela a alguien.
frame: In the ___, you can find ___.
En el ___, puedes encontrar ___.
lookFor: Each page has a layer, an animal and a fact.
Cada página tiene una capa, un animal y un dato.

title: Why Rain Forests Matter
Por qué importan los bosques tropicales
task: Listen. Write down three reasons rain forests are important, then star the one you think matters most.
Escucha. Escribe tres razones por las que los bosques tropicales son importantes y luego marca con una estrella la que te parece más importante.
frame: Rain forests are important because ___. Another reason is ___.
Los bosques tropicales son importantes porque ___. Otra razón es ___.
lookFor: I wrote three facts from the passage.
Escribí tres datos del texto.
squares.listen: Rain forests cover only a small part of Earth's land, but they are home to about half of all the kinds of plants and animals in the world. Rain forest trees take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen, the gas people and animals breathe. Many foods we eat first came from rain forests, such as bananas, cacao for chocolate and cashews. Some medicines come from rain forest plants, too. The Amazon in South America is the largest tropical rain forest on Earth. For all these reasons, scientists work hard to protect rain forests.

title: Two Rain Forests
Dos bosques tropicales
task: Read the text. Draw a Venn diagram and write how tropical and temperate rain forests are alike and different.
Lee el texto. Dibuja un diagrama de Venn y escribe en qué se parecen y en qué se diferencian los bosques tropicales lluviosos y los bosques templados lluviosos.
frame: Both rain forests ___. A tropical rain forest ___, but a temperate rain forest ___.
Los dos bosques ___. Un bosque tropical ___, pero un bosque templado ___.
lookFor: My Venn diagram has at least two facts in each part.
Mi diagrama de Venn tiene por lo menos dos datos en cada parte.
squares.read: Not every rain forest is hot. There are two main kinds. Tropical rain forests grow near the equator, where it is warm all year. Temperate rain forests grow in cooler places, such as along the Pacific coast of North America and in parts of Chile. Both kinds get a lot of rain, and both have tall trees and thick, green plants. In a tropical rain forest, you might see parrots and monkeys. In a temperate rain forest, you might see huge evergreen trees covered in moss, along with elk, salamanders and banana slugs.

title: Compare Two Animals
Compara dos animales
task: Choose two rain forest animals from this board. Tell someone two ways they are alike and two ways they are different.
Elige dos animales del bosque tropical de este tablero. Dile a alguien dos formas en que se parecen y dos en que se diferencian.
frame: Both ___ and ___ ___. However, ___.
Tanto el ___ como el ___ ___. Sin embargo, ___.
lookFor: I gave two likenesses and two differences.
Di dos semejanzas y dos diferencias.

title: Fact File
Ficha de datos
task: Write a paragraph of 3 to 5 sentences comparing the canopy and the forest floor. Use both, also and another.
Escribe un párrafo de 3 a 5 oraciones que compare el dosel y el suelo del bosque. Usa los dos, también y otro.
frame: The canopy ___. The forest floor ___. Both ___.
El dosel ___. El suelo del bosque ___. Los dos ___.
lookFor: My paragraph compares the two layers with signal words.
Mi párrafo compara las dos capas con palabras de transición.

title: What Makes a Shadow
Qué forma una sombra
task: Listen. Then explain to someone how a shadow forms, using because and as a result.
Escucha. Luego explícale a alguien cómo se forma una sombra, usando porque y como resultado.
frame: A shadow forms because ___. As a result, ___.
Una sombra se forma porque ___. Como resultado, ___.
lookFor: I explained the cause and the effect.
Expliqué la causa y el efecto.
squares.listen: Light travels in straight lines. When light hits an object that it cannot pass through, such as your body or a tree, the light is blocked. The area behind the object does not get light, so it looks dark. This dark area is a shadow. A shadow always forms on the side of the object that is away from the light. If you stand with the sun in front of you, your shadow falls behind you. If the sun is behind you, your shadow stretches out in front of you.

title: Shadows All Day
Sombras todo el día
task: Read the text. Draw a flagpole three times, for morning, noon and late afternoon, with the sun and the shadow in the right place each time.
Lee el texto. Dibuja un asta de bandera tres veces, para la mañana, el mediodía y la tarde, con el sol y la sombra en el lugar correcto cada vez.
frame: In the morning, the shadow is ___ because the sun is ___.
En la mañana, la sombra es ___ porque el sol está ___.
lookFor: My three drawings show long, short and long shadows on the correct sides.
Mis tres dibujos muestran sombras largas, cortas y largas en los lados correctos.
squares.read: Every day the sun seems to move across the sky. It is really Earth that is turning, but from the ground, the sun looks like it rises in the east and sets in the west. As the sun moves, shadows change. In the morning, the sun is low in the east, so shadows are long and point west. Around noon, the sun is high in the sky. As a result, shadows are short. In the late afternoon, the sun is low in the west, so shadows grow long again and point east.

title: Shadow Puppets
Títeres de sombra
task: Use a lamp or flashlight and your hands to make a shadow on a wall. Move your hand closer to the light and farther away, then explain what happens and why.
Usa una lámpara o una linterna y tus manos para hacer una sombra en la pared. Acerca y aleja la mano de la luz y luego explica qué pasa y por qué.
frame: When my hand moves closer to the light, the shadow ___ because ___.
Cuando acerco la mano a la luz, la sombra ___ porque ___.
lookFor: I explained how distance changes the shadow.
Expliqué cómo la distancia cambia la sombra.

title: Explain It in Writing
Explícalo por escrito
task: Write a paragraph of 3 to 5 sentences that explains why your shadow is short at noon and long in the evening. Use because, when and as a result.
Escribe un párrafo de 3 a 5 oraciones que explique por qué tu sombra es corta al mediodía y larga en la tarde. Usa porque, cuando y como resultado.
frame: At noon, the sun is ___, so ___. When the sun is low, ___. As a result, ___.
Al mediodía, el sol está ___, así que ___. Cuando el sol está bajo, ___. Como resultado, ___.
lookFor: My paragraph links the sun's position to the shadow's length.
Mi párrafo relaciona la posición del sol con el largo de la sombra.

title: Shadow Tracker
Rastreador de sombras
task: Stand an object, like a cup or a toy, by a sunny window on a paper. Trace its shadow in the morning and again in the afternoon. Label each tracing and explain the change to someone.
Pon un objeto, como un vaso o un juguete, sobre un papel junto a una ventana con sol. Traza su sombra en la mañana y otra vez en la tarde. Rotula cada trazo y explícale el cambio a alguien.
frame: The shadow moved because ___.
La sombra se movió porque ___.
lookFor: My tracings are labeled and I explained the cause.
Mis trazos tienen rótulos y expliqué la causa.

title: The Sundial
El reloj de sol
task: Listen. Then put the steps for how a sundial works in order and say them to someone.
Escucha. Luego pon en orden los pasos de cómo funciona un reloj de sol y díselos a alguien.
frame: First, the sun ___. Then the shadow ___. This causes ___.
Primero, el sol ___. Luego la sombra ___. Esto causa ___.
lookFor: I told the steps in the right order.
Dije los pasos en el orden correcto.
squares.listen: Long ago, before clocks, people used shadows to tell time. A sundial is a flat plate with a pointer that sticks up from the middle. When the sun shines on the pointer, it makes a shadow on the plate. The plate has marks for each hour of the day. As the sun moves across the sky, the shadow moves from one mark to the next. People read the time by looking at which mark the shadow touches. Because a sundial needs the sun, it does not work at night or on cloudy days.

title: Shadow Science
Ciencia de sombras
task: Read the text. Fill in a cause-and-effect chart with two rows: what changes the size of a shadow and what happens.
Lee el texto. Completa una tabla de causa y efecto con dos filas: qué cambia el tamaño de una sombra y qué pasa.
frame: When ___, the shadow becomes ___.
Cuando ___, la sombra se vuelve ___.
lookFor: My chart has two causes, each with its effect.
Mi tabla tiene dos causas, cada una con su efecto.
squares.read: The size of a shadow depends on where the light is. When a light is close to an object, the object blocks more of the light. This causes a large shadow. When the light moves farther away, the shadow becomes smaller and sharper. The angle of the light matters too. When light shines from straight above, it makes a short shadow. When light shines from a low angle, from the side, the shadow stretches out and becomes long. That is why your shadow can look like a giant at sunset.

title: Be the Teacher
Sé el maestro
task: Use a flashlight and a toy to teach someone at home why shadows change length. Show and say each step: what you do, what happens, and why.
Usa una linterna y un juguete para enseñarle a alguien en casa por qué las sombras cambian de largo. Muestra y di cada paso: qué haces, qué pasa y por qué.
frame: When I hold the light ___, the shadow ___. This happens because ___.
Cuando sostengo la luz ___, la sombra ___. Esto pasa porque ___.
lookFor: I showed and explained at least two changes.
Mostré y expliqué por lo menos dos cambios.

title: Answer a Question
Responde una pregunta
task: A younger child asks, Why does my shadow follow me? Write a paragraph of 3 to 5 sentences that answers the question step by step.
Un niño más pequeño pregunta: ¿Por qué me sigue mi sombra? Escribe un párrafo de 3 a 5 oraciones que responda la pregunta paso a paso.
frame: Your shadow follows you because ___. When you move, ___. So ___.
Tu sombra te sigue porque ___. Cuando te mueves, ___. Así que ___.
lookFor: My answer explains the cause in simple steps.
Mi respuesta explica la causa en pasos sencillos.

theme: Should our class have a garden?

title: The Garden Debate
El debate del huerto
task: Listen to two students. Make a T-chart for For and Against and list each reason on the correct side. Then decide whose reasons are stronger.
Escucha a dos estudiantes. Haz una tabla en T para A favor y En contra y escribe cada razón en el lado correcto. Luego decide qué razones son más fuertes.
frame: ___ is for the garden because ___. ___ is against it because ___.
___ está a favor del huerto porque ___. ___ está en contra porque ___.
lookFor: Every reason is on the right side, and I picked the stronger side.
Cada razón está en el lado correcto y elegí el lado más fuerte.
squares.listen: Nia believes our class should start a garden. She says that growing vegetables would teach us about plants better than any book. She also says that kids who grow vegetables are more likely to eat them. Eli disagrees. He thinks a garden would be too much work. He points out that someone would need to water it every day, even on weekends and during summer break. He also worries that our school yard does not get enough sun. That is why he believes we should grow a few plants in pots inside instead.

title: A Teacher's Proposal
La propuesta de un maestro
task: Read the proposal. Write the opinion in one sentence, then list each reason with the fact or example that supports it.
Lee la propuesta. Escribe la opinión en una oración y luego haz una lista de cada razón con el dato o el ejemplo que la apoya.
frame: The opinion is ___. One reason is ___. For example, ___.
La opinión es ___. Una razón es ___. Por ejemplo, ___.
lookFor: Each reason on my list has support.
Cada razón de mi lista tiene apoyo.
squares.read: I believe our class should plant a garden this spring. One reason is that a garden is a real science lab. Students can measure how tall plants grow and test which spot gets the most sun. Another reason is that gardens help the community. For example, our class could give extra vegetables to families in our neighborhood. A garden can also be small. Four wooden boxes would fit next to the playground. Families have already offered to water it during the summer. That is why I think a class garden is a good idea.

title: Make Your Case
Presenta tu caso
task: Tell someone at home whether your class should have a garden. State your opinion, give two reasons with an example for each, and say your opinion again at the end.
Dile a alguien en casa si tu clase debería tener un huerto. Di tu opinión, da dos razones con un ejemplo para cada una y repite tu opinión al final.
frame: I believe ___. One reason is ___. For example, ___. That is why ___.
Creo que ___. Una razón es ___. Por ejemplo, ___. Por eso ___.
lookFor: I stated my opinion, gave supported reasons and restated it.
Di mi opinión, razones con apoyo y la repetí al final.

title: Opinion Paragraph
Párrafo de opinión
task: Write a paragraph of 3 to 5 sentences for or against a class garden. Use I think, one reason, another reason and that is why.
Escribe un párrafo de 3 a 5 oraciones a favor o en contra de un huerto en la clase. Usa pienso que, una razón, otra razón y por eso.
frame: I think ___. One reason is ___. Another reason is ___. That is why ___.
Pienso que ___. Una razón es ___. Otra razón es ___. Por eso ___.
lookFor: My paragraph has an opinion, two reasons and a closing.
Mi párrafo tiene una opinión, dos razones y un cierre.

title: Garden Ad
Anuncio del huerto
