task: Make a mini poster that tries to convince your class to vote yes or no on a garden. Include a slogan, a drawing and two reasons. Read it aloud like an announcer.
Haz un mini cartel que trate de convencer a tu clase de votar sí o no por un huerto. Incluye un lema, un dibujo y dos razones. Léelo en voz alta como un locutor.
frame: Vote ___ because ___!
¡Vota ___ porque ___!

title: The Principal Responds

task: Listen to the principal. Write the concern she has, then write one way a student could answer it.

squares.listen: Thank you for your letter about a class garden. I like that you want to learn outside. However, I have one big concern. Gardens need care every single day. Plants can dry out in just a few hot days. During summer break, the school is closed for many weeks. If no one waters the garden, the plants will die and our hard work will be wasted. Before I can say yes, I need a plan. Please tell me who will take care of the garden when school is out. I look forward to reading your ideas.

title: Which Reason Wins?

squares.read: Three students wrote reasons for a class garden. Reason 1: Gardens are pretty, and I like flowers. Reason 2: In a garden, we could practice math by measuring plant growth each week and making graphs of our results. Reason 3: My cousin's school has a garden, so we should have one too. A strong reason connects to the goal and can be supported with facts or examples. A weak reason is only about what one person likes or what someone else has. Which reason best shows that a garden would help our class learn?

task: Listen to the narrative. Note the exact moment the narrator's feelings shift, then retell the story to someone using three of the time signals you heard.

Identifiqué el momento clave y usé tres expresiones de tiempo en orden.
squares.listen: Earlier that day, I had almost convinced my mom to let me skip soccer tryouts. We had moved to the city only two weeks before, and I did not know a single person on the field. I stood at the edge of the grass, pretending to tie my shoe for the third time. Meanwhile, the other girls were laughing and passing the ball as if they had played together forever. Without warning, a ball rolled straight to my feet. A tall girl with braids jogged over and said, Nice, can you send it back? I kicked it harder than I meant to, and it sailed over her head. I wanted to disappear. Instead, she grinned and shouted, Okay, you are definitely on my side. From that moment on, the field felt a little less like a strange country and a little more like home.

title: Lunch Table

task: Read the narrative. Mark where the setting shifts in time or place, then write one sentence explaining why the author ends with the reflection.

squares.read: The cafeteria was the loudest room I had ever been in. On my first day at Lincoln Middle School, I carried my tray in a slow circle, searching for an empty seat that did not feel like a test. Eventually, I sat at the end of a table near the windows, beside a boy reading a graphic novel. For ten minutes, neither of us spoke. Then I noticed that the book was one my older brother had sent me from Manila. I said, The ending will surprise you. He looked up, suspicious, and asked how I knew. By the time the bell rang, we had argued about every character. Looking back, I realize that the hardest part of being new is not finding a seat. It is finding the one sentence that turns a stranger into someone you know.

Mi historia tuvo contexto, una complicación y una reflexión.

Escribe un párrafo que narre el primer encuentro entre dos personajes en el primer día de alguien. Desarrolla a cada personaje con al menos dos líneas de diálogo y una acción.

squares.listen: On my first morning in our new town, I climbed onto bus 14 instead of bus 41. I did not notice my mistake until the bus turned away from the river and headed toward the hills. My phone was at home charging, and I could feel my face burning. As soon as the bus stopped, I walked up to the driver and explained, in my careful English, that I was lost. She did not laugh. Instead, she pulled out a paper map, traced the route with her finger, and showed me where to switch buses. Meanwhile, an older man in the front row told me that he had done the exact same thing when he first arrived. Eventually, I reached school forty minutes late. Looking back, I am almost glad it happened, because I learned that asking for help is not the same as failing.

squares.read: Tomas had practiced the sentence all weekend: My name is Tomas, and I like to draw. When Mrs. Chen asked the new students to introduce themselves, his mind went completely blank. He stared at his shoes while the class waited. Meanwhile, Mrs. Chen noticed his sketchbook, its cover full of tiny dragons. She did not call on him again. Instead, at the end of the period, she quietly asked if he would design the cover for the class newsletter. Tomas nodded so fast that his glasses slipped. That night, he drew for three hours. When the newsletter came out the following week, his dragons curled around the title. Several classmates asked him to teach them. From that moment on, Tomas did not need a practiced sentence. His drawings introduced him.

title: Renewable vs. Nonrenewable
Renovable y no renovable
task: Listen. Build a two-column chart that classifies each energy source you hear as renewable or nonrenewable, with a one-line definition at the top of each column.
Escucha. Haz una tabla de dos columnas que clasifique cada fuente de energía que escuches como renovable o no renovable, con una definición de una línea arriba de cada columna.
frame: ___ is classified as ___ because ___.
___ se clasifica como ___ porque ___.
lookFor: Every source is in the right column and each column is defined.
Cada fuente está en la columna correcta y cada columna tiene definición.
squares.listen: Energy sources are usually classified into two groups. Renewable energy refers to energy that comes from sources nature replaces quickly, such as sunlight, wind, moving water and heat from inside Earth. Because these sources are constantly renewed, people cannot use them up. Nonrenewable energy, in contrast, comes from sources that take millions of years to form, such as coal, oil and natural gas. These are called fossil fuels because they formed from the remains of ancient plants and animals. Once they are burned, they are gone. In addition, burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, a gas that traps heat in the atmosphere. Overall, the main difference between the two groups is time: renewable sources refill on a human timescale, whereas nonrenewable sources do not. That difference shapes how countries plan for the future.

title: How Solar Panels Work
Cómo funcionan los paneles solares
task: Read the text. Draw and label a diagram of a solar panel system that shows the path of energy from the sun to a home.
Lee el texto. Dibuja y rotula un diagrama de un sistema de paneles solares que muestre el camino de la energía desde el sol hasta una casa.
frame: Solar panels convert ___ into ___. Similarly, ___.
Los paneles solares convierten ___ en ___. De manera similar, ___.
lookFor: My diagram shows each part in order with accurate labels.

squares.read: Solar energy refers to energy that comes from sunlight. A solar panel is made of many small units called solar cells, which are usually made of silicon. When sunlight strikes a solar cell, it knocks tiny particles called electrons loose. The moving electrons create an electric current. The panel produces a type of electricity called direct current, but homes use alternating current. Therefore, a device called an inverter changes the electricity into a form that lights, refrigerators and computers can use. Solar panels can be placed on rooftops, in large fields called solar farms, or even on small devices such as calculators. However, panels produce no electricity at night and less on cloudy days. For this reason, some systems store extra energy in batteries for later use. Overall, solar power turns light into electricity without burning any fuel.

title: Wind Power

task: Listen. Write the steps of how a wind turbine produces electricity, then name one place where turbines work best and why.
Escucha. Escribe los pasos de cómo una turbina eólica produce electricidad y luego nombra un lugar donde las turbinas funcionan mejor y por qué.

lookFor: My steps are in order and I named a location with a reason.

squares.listen: Wind power refers to electricity made from moving air. Wind is created when the sun heats Earth's surface unevenly, so warm air rises and cooler air rushes in to replace it. A modern wind turbine has long blades, such as the three blades you may have seen on a tall white tower. When the wind pushes the blades, they turn a shaft connected to a generator. The generator converts the motion into electricity, which travels through power lines to homes and businesses. Turbines work best in places where the wind is strong and steady, such as open plains, hilltops and coastlines. Some turbines are even built offshore, in the ocean, where winds are stronger. In contrast to solar panels, turbines can produce power at night, although they stop when the wind is too weak.

title: Energy From Earth and Water
Energía de la Tierra y del agua
task: Read the text. Create a comparison table for hydropower and geothermal energy with rows for source, how it works, where it is used and one limitation.
Lee el texto. Crea una tabla comparativa para la energía hidroeléctrica y la geotérmica con filas para fuente, cómo funciona, dónde se usa y una limitación.

lookFor: Every cell of my table has accurate information from the text.

squares.read: Hydropower refers to electricity generated by moving water. Most hydropower plants use a dam to hold back a river, creating a lake called a reservoir. When water is released, it flows through tunnels and spins turbines connected to generators. Hydropower is one of the oldest and largest sources of renewable electricity in the world. However, dams can flood land and change the habitats of fish and other river animals. Geothermal energy, in contrast, comes from heat stored deep inside Earth. In some places, hot water and steam rise close to the surface. Power plants pipe this steam to spin turbines, and some homes use the warm water for heating. Iceland, which sits on a zone of volcanic activity, heats most of its homes with geothermal energy. Overall, both sources are renewable, but each depends on a specific geography.

task: Pretend a neighbor asks, What is the difference between renewable and nonrenewable energy? Answer in an organized way: define each term, give two examples of each, and summarize.
Imagina que un vecino pregunta: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre la energía renovable y la no renovable? Responde de forma organizada: define cada término, da dos ejemplos de cada uno y resume.

Usando al menos dos textos de este tablero, escribe un párrafo que resuma qué es la energía renovable y cómo funcionan dos fuentes. Indica de qué texto viene cada dato.

title: The Tilted Earth
La Tierra inclinada
task: Listen. Draw Earth on both sides of the sun with its axis tilted the same way, and label which hemisphere has summer in each position. Explain the cause in one sentence.
Escucha. Dibuja la Tierra a ambos lados del sol con el eje inclinado hacia el mismo lado y rotula qué hemisferio tiene verano en cada posición. Explica la causa en una oración.

Debido a la inclinación de la Tierra, ___, lo que lleva a ___.
lookFor: My diagram keeps the tilt constant and labels both summers correctly.
Mi diagrama mantiene la inclinación constante y rotula bien los dos veranos.
squares.listen: Many people believe that summer happens because Earth is closer to the sun. In fact, Earth is closest to the sun in early January, which is winter in the Northern Hemisphere. Seasons are actually caused by the tilt of Earth's axis, which leans about 23.5 degrees. As Earth orbits the sun, the axis always points in the same direction in space. Consequently, for part of the year the Northern Hemisphere leans toward the sun, and for the other part it leans away. When a hemisphere leans toward the sun, sunlight hits it more directly and the days are longer. As a result, that hemisphere warms up and has summer. Meanwhile, the opposite hemisphere receives slanted light and shorter days, which leads to winter. Spring and fall occur in between, when neither hemisphere leans toward the sun.

title: Direct and Slanted Light
Luz directa e inclinada
task: Read the text. Create a cause-and-effect chain with at least four linked boxes that explains why direct sunlight heats the ground more.
Lee el texto. Crea una cadena de causa y efecto con al menos cuatro cuadros conectados que explique por qué la luz solar directa calienta más el suelo.
frame: When sunlight hits at a low angle, ___. Therefore, ___.

lookFor: Each box in my chain causes the next one.

squares.read: Why does direct sunlight feel hotter than slanted sunlight? Imagine shining a flashlight straight down at a table. The light makes a small, bright circle. Now tilt the flashlight. The same amount of light spreads into a larger, dimmer oval. Sunlight behaves the same way. In summer, the sun is high in the sky, so its rays strike the ground at a steep angle. This means that the energy is concentrated on a smaller area, and that area heats up quickly. In winter, the sun stays lower in the sky. Due to the low angle, the same energy is spread over a much larger area, so each part receives less. In addition, winter days are shorter, which gives the ground fewer hours to absorb heat. Therefore, temperatures drop. The angle of sunlight, not the distance to the sun, is what matters most.

task: Use a flashlight, or a lamp and a ball, to show someone why the angle of light matters. Narrate each step of the demonstration and connect it to Earth's seasons.
Usa una linterna, o una lámpara y una pelota, para mostrarle a alguien por qué importa el ángulo de la luz. Describe cada paso de la demostración y relaciónalo con las estaciones de la Tierra.

Un amigo dice: Hace calor en verano porque la Tierra está más cerca del sol. Escribe un párrafo que explique por qué esto es incorrecto y dé la verdadera cadena de causas.

Construye un modelo de la órbita de la Tierra: usa una lámpara o un sol dibujado en el centro y una pelota o una fruta atravesada por un lápiz como la Tierra. Hazla girar alrededor del sol manteniendo fija la inclinación y explícale a alguien qué pasa en cuatro puntos.

title: Opposite Seasons
Estaciones opuestas
task: Listen. Then explain to someone why a December holiday can be a winter event in one country and a summer beach day in another.
Escucha. Luego explícale a alguien por qué una fiesta de diciembre puede ser un evento de invierno en un país y un día de playa de verano en otro.

lookFor: I explained the cause, not only the effect.

squares.listen: In December, families in Canada might wear heavy coats to celebrate the new year in the snow. At the same moment, families in Argentina or Australia might celebrate at the beach in the middle of summer. How can both be true? The answer is Earth's tilt. In December, the Southern Hemisphere is tilted toward the sun. Consequently, it receives more direct sunlight and longer days, which leads to summer. The Northern Hemisphere, in contrast, is tilted away, so it receives slanted light and short days. In June, the situation reverses. This means that the two hemispheres always have opposite seasons. Places near the equator, such as Ecuador, receive fairly direct sunlight all year, so their temperatures change very little from month to month. Instead of summer and winter, many of these places have a rainy season and a dry season.

title: Reading the Data

task: Read the data and the text. Explain what pattern the data shows and what causes it. Write your explanation in two sentences that begin with According to the data and This is due to.
Lee los datos y el texto. Explica qué patrón muestran los datos y qué lo causa. Escribe tu explicación en dos oraciones que empiecen con Según los datos y Esto se debe a.

squares.read: A class recorded the approximate hours of daylight in a city in the northern United States on four dates. On March 20, the city had about 12 hours of daylight. On June 21, it had about 15 and a half hours. On September 22, it had about 12 hours again. On December 21, it had only about 9 hours. According to the data, daylight is longest in June and shortest in December. This pattern is due to Earth's tilt. In June, the Northern Hemisphere leans toward the sun, so the sun rises earlier, travels higher across the sky, and sets later. In December, it leans away, which leads to short days. In March and September, neither hemisphere leans toward the sun, so day and night are nearly equal everywhere. These two dates are called equinoxes.

Imagina que eres científico en un programa de radio. Explícale a quien llama por qué tenemos estaciones, relacionando al menos tres causas y efectos con palabras de transición precisas.

title: If Earth Had No Tilt

task: Write an explanatory paragraph that predicts what Earth would be like if its axis had no tilt. Support your prediction with the causes explained on this board.

squares.listen: Speaker one, a student: I believe our school should start at 8:30 instead of 7:30. The evidence shows that teenagers need eight to ten hours of sleep each night. However, during puberty, the body naturally shifts sleep later, so most teens cannot fall asleep before about 11 p.m. If we wake up at 6, we are sleep-deprived every day. Doctors have recommended that middle and high schools start at 8:30 or later. Speaker two, a parent: I understand that students are tired. Nevertheless, a later start would cause real problems. Buses are shared with the elementary schools, so changing one schedule changes them all. In addition, many students care for younger siblings or play sports after school. squares.read: Every morning, thousands of students sit in first period with their eyes half closed. Our school should move its start time to 8:30 a.m. First, sleep affects learning. Students who sleep enough remember more of what they study and pay closer attention in class. Second, when some schools have moved their start times later, studies found that students slept more on school nights and were late or absent less often. Some people argue that a later start will interfere with sports and after-school jobs. That is a fair concern. However, teams could practice later in spring and fall, when it stays light, and some schools have adjusted their schedules without canceling activities. Nevertheless, a schedule can be rearranged far more easily than a tired brain can be repaired. Therefore, the school board should vote for a later start.

squares.listen: As the transportation director, I support healthy sleep for students. However, I want the board to understand the cost of a later start. Right now, each of our buses runs three routes every morning: first the high school, then the middle school, and finally the elementary schools. If the middle school starts an hour later, the buses cannot finish all three routes in time. On the other hand, if we simply flip the order, our youngest students would wait at bus stops before sunrise in winter. The other option is to hire more drivers and buy more buses, and that would cost a large amount of money each year. I am not saying no. I am saying that any plan must answer one question: how will every student get to school safely?

squares.read: A student is writing an argument that school should start later. She has collected four pieces of evidence and must choose the best two. Evidence A: My friends and I are always tired in the morning. Evidence B: Doctors who study adolescent health recommend that middle and high schools start no earlier than 8:30 a.m. Evidence C: Studies of schools that moved to later start times found that students slept more on school nights. Evidence D: Everyone knows that sleeping in is the best part of the weekend. Strong evidence comes from reliable sources, applies to many people, and connects directly to the claim. Weak evidence is based on personal feelings or on what everyone supposedly knows. Choosing carefully makes an argument much more convincing to readers who disagree.
